concepts.title: โปรแกรมแรก: REPL, Script, ตัวแปร ชนิดข้อมูล และตัวเลข
concepts.covers: From zero: what a program, source code, interpreter and script are; python3 REPL (>>>) vs Bash ($), exit(), help(); creating and running a .py file with python3; print(); variables as labelled boxes, naming rules (snake_case), reassignment; basic types int, float, str, bool, None and type(); arithmetic + - * / // % **, operator precedence, round(), int()/float()/str() conversion, why 0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3. Example file ~/projects/python-lab/types_demo.py: stores a shop order (item 'ชาไทย', price 45, qty 3, discount 0.1, is_member True, coupon None), prints each value with type(), computes subtotal 135, discount and total, converts 98765 seconds to 27 ชั่วโมง 26 นาที 5 วินาที with // and %, and prints 0.1 + 0.2 and round(0.1 + 0.2, 2). Mistakes: NameError (typo in variable name), SyntaxError (missing quote/parenthesis), IndentationError: unexpected indent, ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10.

concepts.title: String, f-string และการรับ Input จากผู้ใช้
concepts.covers:
Strings as sequences: quotes, escape 
, len(), indexing (0-based, negative), slicing [start:stop:step], immutability; methods strip, lower, upper, title, replace, split, join, startswith, in; f-strings with format specs {x:,.2f}, {p:.1%}, {s:>10}, {n:05d}, {x=}; input() always returns str, converting with int()/float(). Example file ~/projects/python-lab/fstring_demo.py: cleans '  SOMSRI   ใจดี ' into 'Somsri ใจดี' with split/join/title, shows first/last/first-3 characters, formats 1234567.891 as 1,234,567.89 and 0.075 as 7.5%, prints an aligned 3-row receipt table; then a second small file add_two.py that reads two numbers with input() and prints the sum, run with printf '10
20
' | python3 add_two.py so output is deterministic (shows 30, not '1020'). Mistakes: TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str, IndexError: string index out of range, ValueError from int('3.5'), forgetting the f prefix.

concepts.title: ตัดสินใจด้วย if/elif/else และทำซ้ำด้วย Loop (for, while, range, break, continue)
concepts.covers: Comparison and logical operators (==, !=, <, <=, and, or, not, chained 0 <= x <= 100), truthiness of 0, '', [], None; if/elif/else order matters; indentation as block structure; for over a list/string, range(start, stop, step), enumerate(start=1), while with a counter, break, continue, for-else briefly; infinite loops and Ctrl+C. Example file ~/projects/python-lab/grade_loop.py: a function-free script that loops over scores [95, 82, 74, 61, 48, 105] with enumerate, skips invalid scores (>100 or <0) with continue, assigns grades A(>=80)/B(>=70)/C(>=60)/D(>=50)/F, counts passes, stops at the first score of 0 with break (not present, explain), then a while loop simulating 3 PIN attempts from a fixed list ['1111', '2580', '0000'] against correct PIN '1234' ending with 'ล็อกบัญชี'. Mistakes: SyntaxError: expected ':', using = instead of == (SyntaxError: invalid syntax. Maybe you meant '==' or ':=' instead of '='?), wrong elif order giving wrong grade, infinite while loop (forgot to update counter), IndentationError: expected an indented block after 'if' statement.

concepts.title: เก็บข้อมูลหลายค่า: List, Tuple, Set, Dict และ Comprehension
concepts.covers: When to use each: list (ordered, mutable: append, insert, remove, pop, sort vs sorted, in), tuple (fixed records, unpacking lat, lon = (13.7563, 100.5018)), set (unique values, union/intersection/difference), dict (key-value: [], .get(key, default), .items(), .keys(), update, del, nested dict, looping); list/dict/set comprehensions with if filter, and the equivalent plain for loop; list.sort() returns None. Example file ~/projects/python-lab/collections_basics.py using a cart of dicts [{'name': 'ชาไทย', 'price': 45, 'qty': 2}, {'name': 'ข้าวมันไก่', 'price': 50, 'qty': 1}, {'name': 'ขนมปังสังขยา', 'price': 35, 'qty': 3}, {'name': 'น้ำเปล่า', 'price': 10, 'qty': 4}]: total with a loop and with sum() of a generator, sort by price descending with sorted(key=lambda), unique provinces with a set from ['เชียงใหม่', 'ขอนแก่น', 'เชียงใหม่', 'ภูเก็ต'], a phonebook dict with .get('สมชาย', 'ไม่พบ'), and comprehensions {name: price*qty} and [name for ... if price >= 40]. Mistakes: KeyError: 'สมชาย', IndexError: list index out of range, AttributeError: 'tuple' object has no attribute 'append', result = cart.sort() gives None, TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'.

concepts.title: Functions: Parameters, Default, *args/**kwargs, Return, Type Hints และ Docstring
concepts.covers: Why functions (reuse, naming, testing); def, parameters vs arguments, positional and keyword arguments, default values, return vs print (a function without return gives None), multiple return values as a tuple, scope (local vs global), *args and **kwargs, keyword-only parameters after *, type hints (int, float, str, list[float], dict[str, int], X | None) and that Python does not enforce them at runtime, docstrings and help(); the mutable default argument pitfall and the None fix; lambda briefly. Example file ~/projects/python-lab/functions_demo.py: grade(score: int) -> str, average(*numbers: float) -> float that raises ValueError on no input, vat(amount: float, rate: float = 0.07) -> float, describe(name: str, **info: str) -> str, split_bill(total: float, people: int, *, tip: float = 0.0) -> tuple[float, float], add_item_bad(item, basket=[]) vs add_item(item, basket=None) showing the shared-list bug, and printing help(vat) docstring via vat.__doc__. Mistakes: TypeError: grade() missing 1 required positional argument: 'score', TypeError: split_bill() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given, using print instead of return then getting None in a calculation (TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'int'), UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'total' where it is not associated with a value.

concepts.title: Modules, Packages, if __name__ == "__main__", venv, pip และ requirements.txt (พร้อมเรียก HTTP API ในเครื่อง)
concepts.covers: A module is a .py file; import, from ... import, import ... as; a package is a folder with __init__.py; how sys.path finds modules (script folder first, so never name your file random.py, csv.py or requests.py); the if __name__ == '__main__' idiom shown by running a module directly vs importing it. Then packages from PyPI: why Ubuntu 24.04 blocks system pip with 'error: externally-managed-environment' (PEP 668) and the fix: sudo apt install -y python3-venv python3-pip, python3 -m venv .venv, source .venv/bin/activate (prompt shows (.venv)), which python3, python3 -m pip install "requests==2.34.2", python3 -m pip freeze > requirements.txt, deactivate, rebuild with python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt; .venv goes in .gitignore. Runnable example in ~/projects/python-lab/pkg-lab: package thaimoney/ (__init__.py exporting format_baht, convert.py with format_baht(amount: float) -> str returning '1,234.50 บาท' and thb_to(amount, rate) ) and fetch_rates.py that imports thaimoney and requests, fetches http://127.0.0.1:8000/rates.json (same rates.json as Part 1: {"base": "THB", "date": "2026-10-19", "rates": {"USD": 0.0305, "JPY": 4.62, "EUR": 0.0281}}) served by python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 from public/ in Terminal 1, uses timeout=5 and response.raise_for_status(), and prints 1,000 บาท in each currency; status codes 200/404 explained; httpx 0.28.1 named as an alternative with the same get()/json() API (deeper HTTP error handling is in Parts 3/4). Mistakes: error: externally-managed-environment, ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'requests' (venv not activated), ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'thaimoney' (running from the wrong folder), AttributeError: partially initialized module 'random' has no attribute 'randint' (most likely due to a circular import) when a file is named random.py, requests.exceptions.ConnectionError ... Connection refused when the server is not running.

concepts.title: ทำงานกับไฟล์: pathlib, open, csv และ json
concepts.covers: Paths with pathlib.Path (/ operator, .exists(), .mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True), .glob('*.csv'), .read_text/.write_text, .name/.suffix/.stem); open() modes r/w/a and with blocks; always encoding='utf-8' for Thai text and newline='' for csv; csv.DictReader/DictWriter (writeheader, appending a row without losing data); json.dump/json.load with ensure_ascii=False, indent=2. Example file ~/projects/python-lab/read_expenses.py working on ~/projects/python-lab/data/expenses.csv with the exact 8 sample rows (see notes): reads with DictReader, converts amount to float, filters date.startswith('2026-10'), sums per category with a dict, prints the October total 2003.5 and per-category totals {'bills': 1250.5, 'food': 185.0, 'shopping': 299.0, 'transport': 184.0, 'health': 85.0}, writes data/summary-2026-10.json with ensure_ascii=False, reads it back, and lists all .csv files in data/ with glob. Mistakes: FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'data/expenses.csv' (wrong working directory; fix with Path(__file__).parent), UnicodeDecodeError when encoding is missing on files saved by Windows Excel (cp874/utf-8-sig), json showing \u0e04 escapes without ensure_ascii=False, blank lines between rows on Windows without newline='', opening with 'w' instead of 'a' erases the file.

concepts.title: Exceptions และการ Debug: try/except/else/finally, raise, Custom Exception และ pdb
concepts.covers: Reading a Traceback bottom-up (exception type, message, file, line, call chain); common built-in exceptions; try/except with specific types, multiple except, except ... as e, else (runs when no error) and finally (always runs); raise ValueError(...) with a clear message; custom exceptions class InvalidAmountError(ValueError); re-raising with raise ... from e; why bare except: and except Exception: pass are bad. Debugging: print debugging with f'{x=}', breakpoint() which opens pdb (commands n, s, c, p var, l, w, q), PYTHONBREAKPOINT=0 to disable, and the VS Code debugger (F9 breakpoint, F5 Python Debugger: Current File, Variables panel). Example file ~/projects/python-lab/safe_parse.py: parse_amount(text: str) -> float that raises InvalidAmountError for non-numbers, zero or negatives and more than 2 decimals; a loop over inputs ['89.50', 'abc', '-20', '120.555', '1,250.50'] printing OK or the friendly error, using else and finally (count of processed items); plus a pdb session demo shown as a wsl block where the learner runs the script with a breakpoint() and types p text and n then c (show the realistic (Pdb) transcript; values on the learner's machine for paths will be /home/somchai/projects/python-lab/safe_parse.py). Mistakes: catching too broadly and hiding bugs, ValueError: could not convert string to float: 'abc', ZeroDivisionError: division by zero, forgetting to remove breakpoint() before committing, finally swallowing return values.

concepts.title: Standard Library ที่ใช้บ่อย: datetime, collections, itertools, random/secrets, argparse และ logging
concepts.covers: datetime.date/datetime, date.fromisoformat('2026-10-19'), timedelta, strftime('%d/%m/%Y'), days between dates; collections.Counter.most_common(3), defaultdict(float) for group totals, namedtuple briefly; itertools.groupby (needs sorted input), chain, islice, accumulate; random.seed/choice/sample/shuffle for simulations vs secrets.token_urlsafe/choice for passwords and tokens; argparse with a positional argument, --option with type=float and choices, default, help text, and automatic --help; logging.basicConfig with level, format, a FileHandler to app.log at DEBUG and a StreamHandler at WARNING, logger = logging.getLogger(__name__). Example file ~/projects/python-lab/expense_stats.py: an argparse CLI python3 expense_stats.py data/expenses.csv --month 2026-10 --top 3 that reads the sample CSV, uses date.fromisoformat, defaultdict and Counter to print per-category totals, the top-3 categories by count, the number of days between the first and last expense, a running total with itertools.accumulate, logs 'อ่าน 8 รายการ' at INFO to app.log and a WARNING to the screen when a month has no data; show the --help output and a run with --month 2026-12 to trigger the warning. Do not show random output without random.seed(42). Mistakes: ValueError: Invalid isoformat string: '19/10/2026', argparse 'error: argument --top: invalid int value: 'three'', groupby giving split groups on unsorted data, using random for passwords, logging.basicConfig called after the first log message having no effect.

concepts.title: Object-Oriented Programming: Class, Object, Inheritance, @property และ Dataclass
concepts.covers: Class vs object, __init__ and self, attributes and methods, __str__ vs __repr__, class attributes vs instance attributes, inheritance with super().__init__() and method overriding, @property and setter for validation, @classmethod as an alternate constructor, composition over inheritance; @dataclass (auto __init__/__repr__/__eq__, field(default_factory=list), frozen=True, order=True, __post_init__ validation) and when a dataclass beats a dict. Example file ~/projects/python-lab/oop_demo.py: class Account(owner, balance) with deposit/withdraw raising ValueError on overdraft and a read-only balance property; SavingsAccount(Account) adding interest rate and add_interest(); then @dataclass Expense(id: int, date: date, category: str, amount: Decimal, note: str = '') with __post_init__ checking category in CATEGORIES and amount > 0, plus a from_row(cls, row: dict) classmethod that parses one CSV row; prints repr, equality of two Expense objects, sorted by amount. This Expense dataclass is the same model used in the Mini Project. Mistakes: TypeError: Account.deposit() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given (forgot self), AttributeError: property 'balance' of 'Account' object has no setter, forgetting super().__init__() so attributes are missing (AttributeError: 'SavingsAccount' object has no attribute 'owner'), ValueError: mutable default <class 'list'> for field tags is not allowed: use default_factory, FrozenInstanceError: cannot assign to field 'amount'.

concepts.title: Iterator, Generator, Decorator และ Context Manager
concepts.covers: The iteration protocol: iter(), next(), StopIteration, what a for loop does underneath; generator functions with yield, lazy evaluation and memory (sys.getsizeof of a list vs generator for range(1_000_000)), generator expressions, yield from; decorators: functions are objects, closures, writing @timer and @retry(times=3) with *args/**kwargs and functools.wraps, functools.cache on recursive fib(80); context managers: with, a class with __enter__/__exit__, and contextlib.contextmanager. Example file ~/projects/python-lab/advanced_demo.py: read_lines(path) generator that yields non-empty stripped lines from data/expenses.csv lazily and a pipeline of generator expressions summing October amounts (2003.5); manual next() calls until StopIteration; @timer decorator (print elapsed in ms, output varies so mark it as varying and avoid exact digits by printing '<0.1 ms' style or say values differ) and @log_call printing arguments and the result; fib with @functools.cache printing fib(80) = 23416728348467685; a Timer/Section context manager built both as a class and with @contextmanager that prints enter/exit messages and still runs cleanup when an exception happens. Mistakes: reusing an exhausted generator gives nothing, TypeError: 'generator' object is not subscriptable, forgetting functools.wraps so __name__ becomes 'wrapper', decorator that forgets to return the result giving None, RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded without cache/base case.

concepts.title: Testing ด้วย pytest, Code Quality ด้วย ruff และ Big-O ด้วย timeit
concepts.covers: Why automated tests; pytest discovery rules (tests/test_*.py, def test_*), plain assert, pytest.raises(ValueError, match=...), @pytest.mark.parametrize, fixtures and tmp_path, pytest.approx for floats, pyproject.toml with [tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath = ["."] and testpaths; reading a failing test report; ruff check (rules E, F, I, B, UP), ruff check --fix, ruff format and --check, configured in pyproject.toml with target-version = "py312" and line-length = 88. Big-O intuition: O(1) dict/set lookup vs O(n) list search, O(log n) binary search, O(n^2) nested loops, O(n log n) sorted(); measuring with timeit.timeit(number=...). Example project ~/projects/python-lab/testing-lab (same folder as Part 1): algorithms.py with linear_search, binary_search (returns index or -1), find_common_slow (nested loops) and find_common_fast (set), and tests/test_algorithms.py with at least 8 tests including parametrize, edge cases (empty list, first/last element, not found) and pytest.raises for unsorted input check; bench.py comparing find_common_slow vs find_common_fast on two lists of 5,000 ints and 'x in list' vs 'x in set' with timeit (timings vary by machine: say so). Install inside .venv: python3 -m pip install "pytest==9.1.1" "ruff==0.17.1". Show real pytest -v output (header shows platform linux, Python version will read 3.12.3 on the learner's machine and pytest-9.1.1, pluggy-1.7.0), a deliberately failing test's assertion report, and ruff check output before and after --fix. Mistakes: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'algorithms' when pythonpath is not set, 'collected 0 items' because file or function names don't start with test_, assert 0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3 failing without pytest.approx, ruff F401 [*] `os` imported but unused, I001 [*] Import block is un-sorted or un-formatted.

mini_project.name: Expense Tracker CLI
mini_project.summary: A portfolio-quality command line app run with python3 -m expense_tracker that records personal expenses in data/expenses.csv, supports add/list/edit/delete/summary/export subcommands via argparse, validates every input with friendly Thai error messages and correct exit codes (0 success, 1 data/validation error, 2 argparse usage error), exports JSON with readable Thai, has a pytest suite of at least 12 tests using tmp_path, passes ruff check and ruff format --check, and installs from a pinned requirements.txt. Folder ~/projects/expense-tracker.
features: add --date YYYY-MM-DD --category <one of CATEGORIES> --amount <Decimal > 0, max 2 decimals> [--note TEXT]; new id = max existing id + 1; --date defaults to today
list [--month YYYY-MM] [--category CAT] prints an aligned table (id, date, category, amount with 2 decimals, note) and a total line
edit ID [--date] [--category] [--amount] [--note] updates only given fields; unknown id prints 'ไม่พบรายการ id 99' and exits 1
delete ID removes one row; unknown id exits 1

summary --month YYYY-MM prints per-category totals sorted by amount descending plus the month total; with the 8 sample rows, --month 2026-10 gives bills 1,250.50 / shopping 299.00 / food 185.00 / transport 184.00 / health 85.00 / รวม 2,003.50 บาท

export [--month YYYY-MM] --output exports/expenses-2026-10.json writes a JSON list of objects with ensure_ascii=False, indent=2, amounts as strings like "1250.50" to keep Decimal precision, creating the parent folder
Validation: bad date -> 'วันที่ต้องอยู่ในรูปแบบ YYYY-MM-DD', amount <= 0 or more than 2 decimals -> clear message, unknown category -> argparse choices error; no Traceback shown to the user

Package layout expense_tracker/{__init__.py,__main__.py,cli.py,models.py,storage.py,report.py}; storage functions take a Path so tests use tmp_path; the CSV path defaults to data/expenses.csv and can be overridden by --file or the environment variable EXPENSES_FILE
Tests: tests/test_models.py, test_storage.py, test_report.py, test_cli.py (calls cli.main(argv) and checks capsys output and exit codes), at least 12 tests in total, all passing

Tooling: pyproject.toml with [tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath=["."], testpaths=["tests"] and [tool.ruff] target-version="py312", line-length=88, lint select E,F,I,B,UP; requirements.txt pinning pytest==9.1.1 and ruff==0.17.1; .gitignore with .venv/, __pycache__/, .pytest_cache/, .ruff_cache/, exports/; README.md; pushed to GitHub as somchai/expense-tracker
mini_project.stack: Python 3.12.3 (system python3 on Ubuntu 24.04; code must also run on 3.13); standard library only at runtime: argparse, csv, json, pathlib, dataclasses, datetime, decimal, collections, sys, os; dev tools in .venv: pytest 9.1.1 (pluggy 1.7.0), ruff 0.17.1; pip 24.0; Git 2.43.0 and GitHub

versions.apt_packages: python3-venv python3-pip (sudo apt install -y python3-venv python3-pip)

notes: Username is somchai; home is /home/somchai. Practice folder for Parts 2-3 is ~/projects/python-lab (with its own .venv at ~/projects/python-lab/.venv created in Part 2 setup). Sub-folders: ~/projects/python-lab/data, ~/projects/python-lab/pkg-lab (c06), ~/projects/python-lab/pkg-lab/public (rates.json for http.server), ~/projects/python-lab/testing-lab (c12). Sample data file data/expenses.csv (UTF-8, header id,date,category,amount,note) has exactly these 8 rows, used everywhere: 1,2026-09-28,food,50.00,ข้าวมันไก่ | 2,2026-09-30,transport,47.00,BTS ไปทำงาน | 3,2026-10-01,bills,1250.50,ค่าไฟฟ้า | 4,2026-10-02,food,65.00,กาแฟเย็น | 5,2026-10-03,shopping,299.00,เสื้อยืด | 6,2026-10-05,transport,184.00,Grab กลับบ้าน | 7,2026-10-07,food,120.00,ส้มตำไก่ย่าง | 8,2026-10-10,health,85.00,ยาแก้แพ้. October 2026 total = 2003.50 (bills 1250.50, shopping 299.00, food 185.00, transport 184.00, health 85.00); September total = 97.00. The Mini Project example adds id 9: 2026-10-12, food, 89.50, ข้าวกะเพราไก่ (then edit 9 --amount 95, delete 9).

CATEGORIES (fixed, in this order): food, transport, bills, shopping, health, entertainment, other. Display names in Thai when needed: food=อาหาร, transport=เดินทาง, bills=ค่าบริการ/บิล, shopping=ช้อปปิ้ง, health=สุขภาพ, entertainment=บันเทิง, other=อื่นๆ (write the Thai word อื่นๆ only as a category label value; never as a summarising phrase).
Money: in the Mini Project and c10 use decimal.Decimal (Decimal('89.50')), never float; earlier beginner concepts may use float and explain the float pitfall. Format money as f'{amount:,.2f} บาท'.
Today's date in examples is 2026-10-19 (Python's date.today() output varies; say so). Use random.seed(42) whenever random output is shown.

Local API: rates.json = {"base": "THB", "date": "2026-10-19", "rates": {"USD": 0.0305, "JPY": 4.62, "EUR": 0.0281}} served with python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 in a second terminal; URL http://127.0.0.1:8000/rates.json. Optional API key env var name: RATES_API_KEY; when missing, code falls back to the local/mock data automatically. Never hard-code keys.

Always run scripts as python3 file.py (not python). Install packages only inside an activated venv with python3 -m pip install "pkg==x.y.z". Show the (.venv) prompt prefix in wsl blocks when the venv is active, e.g. (.venv) somchai@DESKTOP:~/projects/python-lab$ only in output blocks; command blocks contain commands only.

Outputs that vary (timings, memory addresses, paths, dates, pytest timing 'in 0.03s') must be shown realistically and labelled in Thai as values that differ on the learner's machine. pytest header should read 'platform linux -- Python 3.12.3, pytest-9.1.1, pluggy-1.7.0' and rootdir /home/somchai/... (the sandbox runs 3.13; adjust the header line and say so).

Terminology (keep English): Script, REPL, Interpreter, Variable, Function, Parameter, Argument, Return value, Module, Package, Virtual Environment (venv), Exception, Traceback, Class, Object, Method, Attribute, Dataclass, Iterator, Generator, Decorator, Context Manager, Test, Fixture, Linter, Formatter, Big-O, Subcommand. Python file names use snake_case; folders use kebab-case except Python packages (snake_case).

Code style in all parts: ruff-clean (line length 88), type hints on all functions from c05 onward, Thai comments, double quotes, f-strings, pathlib over os.path, with-blocks for files, encoding="utf-8" on every open().
